source_units_read.text: The utterance against Damascus. Behold, Damascus will be removed from the cities and become a ruin,
abandoned for everlasting time, a bed and resting place for flocks, with no one pursuing.

There will no longer be a stronghold for Ephraim to flee to, nor a kingdom in Damascus, and the Syrians’ remainder will perish; for you are no better than Israel’s sons and their glory. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.
On that day Jacob’s glory will fail, and the fat parts of his glory will be shaken.
It will be as when someone gathers a standing harvest and reaps seed from the ears in his arm, as when someone gathers an ear in a firm ravine,
and a stalk is left in it, or like olive berries, two or three on a lofty top, or four or five left on their branches. Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God.
On that day a person will trust in the One who made him, and his eyes will look toward Israel’s Holy One,
and they will certainly not trust the altars or their hands’ works, which their fingers made, nor look at their trees or abominations.
On that day your cities will be abandoned as the Amorites and Hivites abandoned theirs before Israel’s sons, and they will be deserted,
because you abandoned God your Savior and did not remember the Lord your Helper. Therefore you will plant a faithless planting and faithless seed;
on the day you plant, you will wander. In the morning, if you sow, it will blossom for harvest on whatever day you allot, and like a human father you will allot to your sons.
Woe, the multitude of many nations! Like a surging sea, so you will be troubled, and the back of many nations will roar like water.

Many nations are like abundant water, like much water violently rushing down. He will drive him away and pursue him far off, like chaff-dust when people winnow before wind, and like wheel-dust carried by a squall.
Toward evening there will be mourning; before morning it will be gone. This is the portion of those who plundered you, an inheritance for those who took possession of you.
Woe, wings of a land of ships, beyond Ethiopia’s rivers,

the one sending hostages by sea and papyrus letters over the water! For swift messengers will go to a lofty nation and a foreign and harsh people—who is beyond it?—a hopeless and trampled nation. Now the land’s rivers,
all are like an inhabited country; their country will be inhabited as when a signal is raised from a mountain, and it will be audible like a trumpet’s voice.
For thus the Lord said to me, “There will be security in My city, like the light of midday heat, and it will be like a dew cloud on a harvest day.”

Before harvest, when the bloom is complete and the unripe grape blossoms as its flower forms unripe fruit, He will remove the small grape clusters with sickles, remove the vine branches and cut them down,
and leave them together for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts. Heaven’s birds will gather upon them, and all the earth’s wild beasts will come upon him.

At that time gifts will be brought to the Lord Sabaoth from a people afflicted and plucked, and from a great people from now on and for everlasting time—a hoping and trampled nation, which is in a part of its country’s river—to the place where the Lord Sabaoth’s name was called, Mount Zion.
A vision of Egypt. Behold, the Lord sits upon a light cloud and will come into Egypt; Egypt’s handmade objects will be shaken before Him, and their heart overcome within them.
Egyptians will be roused against Egyptians; each will fight his brother and each his neighbor, city against city and district against district.
The Egyptians’ spirit will be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel. They will inquire of their gods, their statues, those speaking from the earth and the belly-speakers.
I will hand Egypt into the hands of harsh human masters, and harsh kings will rule them. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.
The Egyptians will drink water beside the sea, but the river will fail and dry up.
Rivers and the river’s canals will fail, and every gathering of water dry up, in every marsh of reed and papyrus,
and all the green marsh growth around the river and everything sown by the river will dry up, destroyed by wind.
Fishermen will groan, and all casting a hook into the river will groan; those casting seines and those using casting nets will mourn.
Shame will seize those working split flax and those working fine linen,
and those warping them will be in pain, and all who make beer will be grieved and suffer in their souls.
Tanis’s rulers will be fools; the king’s wise counselors—their counsel will become foolish. How will you say to the king, “We are sons of the discerning, sons of kings from the beginning”?
Where are your wise men now? Let them announce to you and say what the Lord Sabaoth has counseled against Egypt.
Tanis’s rulers failed, and Memphis’s rulers were exalted; they will lead Egypt astray tribe by tribe.
For the Lord mixed for them a spirit of wandering; they led Egypt astray in all their works, as someone wanders while drunk and vomiting.
There will be no work for the Egyptians that will produce a head and tail, a beginning and end.
On that day the Egyptians will be like women in fear and trembling before the Lord Sabaoth’s hand, which He Himself will bring upon them.
The Judeans’ country will become a terror to the Egyptians; whenever anyone names her to them, they will fear because of the counsel the Lord has counseled against her.
On that day five cities in Egypt will speak the Canaanite language and swear by the Lord’s name. One city will be called City-Asedek.
On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the Egyptians’ country and a pillar to the Lord by its border,

and it will be an everlasting sign to the Lord in Egypt’s country, because they will cry to the Lord on account of their oppressors. The Lord will send them a man who will save them; judging, he will save them.
The Lord will be known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day. They will make sacrifices, vow vows to the Lord and pay them.
The Lord will strike the Egyptians with a great blow and heal them with healing. They will turn back to the Lord, and He will listen to them and heal them.
On that day there will be a road from Egypt toward the Assyrians. Assyrians will enter Egypt, and Egyptians go toward the Assyrians, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians.
On that day Israel will be third among the Assyrians and Egyptians, blessed upon the earth,
which the Lord Sabaoth blessed, saying, “Blessed be My people in Egypt and among the Assyrians, and My inheritance Israel.”
In the year Tanathan entered Azotus, when he was sent by Arna king of the Assyrians and fought Azotus and seized it,
then the Lord spoke to Isaiah, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and untie the sandals on your feet.” He did so, going naked and without sandals.
The Lord said, “As Isaiah My servant has gone naked and without sandals for three years, there will be signs and wonders for the Egyptians and Ethiopians;
for thus the king of the Assyrians will lead Egypt’s and the Ethiopians’ captivity, young men and elders, naked and without sandals, exposed as Egypt’s shame.
The Egyptians will be ashamed in defeat because of the Ethiopians, in whom the Egyptians had trusted, for they were their glory.
Those dwelling on this island will say, ‘Behold, we had trusted that we could flee to them for help, but they could not be saved from the king of the Assyrians. How, then, shall we be saved?’”
The vision of the wilderness. As a squall might pass through a wilderness, coming from a wilderness, from a land—a fearsome

and harsh vision was announced to me. The faithless person deals faithlessly, and the lawless person acts lawlessly. The Elamites are against me, and Persian envoys come against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.
Therefore my loins filled with weakness, and labor pains seized me like a woman giving birth. I did wrong by not hearing; I strove not to see.
My heart wanders, and lawlessness submerges me; my soul stands in fear.
Prepare the table; drink, eat! Rise, rulers; prepare shields!
For thus the Lord said to me: “Go, station a watcher for yourself, and report whatever you see.
I saw mounted riders, two horsemen, a donkey rider and a camel rider. Listen with great attention,
and call Uriah to the Lord’s watchtower.” He said, “I stood continually by day, and at the camp I stood all night,
and behold, he himself comes, a rider of a two-horse team.” He answered and said, “Babylon has fallen, and all her statues and handmade objects were shattered to the ground.”
Hear, you who remain and suffer; hear what I heard from the Lord Sabaoth. Israel’s God announced it to us.
The vision of Idumea. One calls to me from Seir: “Guard the battlements.”
“I watch morning and night. If you seek, seek, and dwell beside me;
in the wood you will sleep at evening, on Daidan’s road.”
Bring water to meet the thirsty, you dwelling in Thaiman’s country; meet the fugitives with loaves,
because of the multitude of those fleeing, the multitude of those wandering, the multitude of the sword, the multitude of ready arrows, and the multitude of those fallen in war.
For thus the Lord said to me: “Yet one year, like a hired worker’s year, and the glory of Kedar’s sons will fail,
and the remaining arrows of Kedar’s strong sons will be few, because the Lord, Israel’s God, has spoken.”
The utterance of Zion’s ravine. What happened to you now, that you all went up to the roofs,
the futile roofs? The city was filled with people crying out. Your wounded were not wounded by a sword, nor did your dead die in war.
All your rulers have fled; those captured are harshly bound, and the strong among you have fled far away.
Therefore I said, “Leave me; I will weep bitterly. Do not insist on comforting me over the shattering of the daughter of my race.”
For there is a day of disturbance, destruction, trampling and wandering from the Lord Sabaoth in Zion’s ravine. They wander from small to great; they wander upon the mountains.
The Elamites took quivers—mounted men upon horses and an assembled battle line.
Your chosen ravines will be filled with chariots, and the horsemen will block your gates,
and they will uncover Judah’s gates and look on that day into the city’s choice houses,
and uncover the hidden things of the houses in David’s citadel. They saw that they were many and that the old pool’s water had been diverted into the city,
and that Jerusalem’s houses had been pulled down to fortify the city’s wall.
You provided water for yourselves between the two walls, inside the old pool, and did not look to the One who made her from the beginning or see the One who founded her.
The Lord Sabaoth called on that day for weeping, lamentation, shaving and putting on sackcloth,
but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
These things are revealed in the Lord Sabaoth’s ears: “This sin will not be forgiven you until you die.”
Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: “Go into the chamber to Somnas the treasurer, and say to him,
What are you doing here, and what do you have here, that you quarried yourself a memorial here, made yourself a memorial on high and inscribed yourself a dwelling in rock?
Behold, the Lord Sabaoth will cast out and crush a man and remove your robe,
and your glorious crown, and throw you into a great and immeasurable country. There you will die; He will make your fine chariot dishonored and your ruler’s house a trampling place,
and you will be removed from your stewardship and your standing.
On that day I will call My servant Eliakim, son of Chelkias,
clothe him in your robe, give him your crown, and put the power and your stewardship in his hands. He will be like a father to those dwelling in Jerusalem and those dwelling in Judah.
I will give him David’s glory, and he will rule, with no one contradicting.
I will establish him as a ruler in a trustworthy place, and he will become a throne of glory for his father’s house.
Every glorious person in his father’s house, from small to great, will trust in him, and they will hang upon him.
On that day—thus says the Lord Sabaoth—the person established in a trustworthy place will be shaken and fall, and the glory upon him will be removed, because the Lord has spoken.”
The vision of Tyre. Wail, ships of Carthage, because she has perished, and they no longer come from the Kitians’ land; she has been led captive.
Whom have the island-dwelling traders of Phoenicia become like, crossing the sea
upon much water, seed of traders? Like a harvest being brought in are the nations’ traders.
“Be ashamed, Sidon,” said the sea; and the sea’s strength said, “I did not labor or give birth or rear young men or raise maidens.”
When it becomes known to Egypt, pain will seize them concerning Tyre.
Go away to Carthage! Wail, residents of this island!
Was this not your insolence from the beginning, before she was handed over?
Who planned these things against Tyre? Is she weaker, or has she no strength? Her merchants are glorious, rulers of the earth.
The Lord Sabaoth planned it, to dissolve all the insolence of the glorious and dishonor everything glorious upon the earth.
Work your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage.
Your hand no longer has strength at sea, the hand that provoked kings. The Lord Sabaoth commanded concerning Canaan, to destroy her strength.
They will say, “You shall no longer continue in insolence and in wronging Sidon’s daughter.” Even if you go to the Kitians, there too you will have no rest,
and into the Chaldeans’ land: this too has been devastated by the Assyrians. There too you will have no rest, because her wall has fallen.
Wail, ships of Carthage, because your fortress has perished!
On that day Tyre will be left for seventy years, like a king’s time, like a person’s time. After seventy years, Tyre will be like a prostitute’s song:
“Take a lyre, wander through cities, forgotten prostitute! Play the lyre well, sing much, so that you may be remembered.”
After seventy years God will visit Tyre, and she will again be restored to her former state and become a trading center for all the inhabited world’s kingdoms.

Her trade and her wage will be holy to the Lord. It will not be collected for them; instead, all her trade will be for those dwelling before the Lord, to eat and drink and be filled, as a contribution, a memorial before the Lord.
Behold, the Lord is destroying the inhabited world; He will make it desolate, uncover its face and scatter those dwelling in it.

The people will be like the priest, the slave like the master, the maidservant like the mistress; the buyer will be like the seller, the lender like the borrower, and the debtor like the one to whom he owes a debt.
The earth will be utterly destroyed, and the earth utterly plundered, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken these things.
The earth mourned, the inhabited world was destroyed, and the earth’s high ones mourned.
The earth acted lawlessly because of those dwelling in it, because they transgressed the law and changed the ordinances, an everlasting covenant.
Therefore a curse will consume the earth, because those dwelling in it sinned. Therefore those dwelling on the earth will be poor, and few people will be left.
Wine will mourn, the vine will mourn, and all who gladden the soul will groan.
The joy of tambourines has ceased; the impudence and wealth of the ungodly have ceased; the lyre’s sound has ceased.
They were ashamed and did not drink wine; sikera became bitter to those drinking it.
Every city was deserted; he will shut a house so that none may enter.
Wail over wine everywhere! All the earth’s gladness has ceased.
Cities will be left deserted, and abandoned houses will perish.
All these things will happen on the earth, among the nations: as when someone gleans an olive tree, so they will glean them, even when the grape harvest has ceased.
These will cry aloud, and those left upon the earth will rejoice together with the Lord’s glory. The sea’s water will be troubled;
therefore the Lord’s glory will be in the sea’s islands; the Lord’s name will be glorious—O Lord, Israel’s God!
From the earth’s wings we heard wonders: “Hope for the devout!” And they will say, “Woe to those who reject, those who reject the law!”
Fear, pit and trap are upon you who dwell on the earth!
Whoever flees the fear will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught by the trap, because windows from heaven have opened and the earth’s foundations will be shaken.
The earth will be utterly agitated, and the earth will be utterly at a loss;
The earth has tilted and will be shaken like a fruit-watcher’s shelter, like someone drunk and hungover. It will fall and will never be able to rise, for lawlessness has prevailed upon it.
God will bring His hand against heaven’s array and against the earth’s kings.
They will gather and shut them into a fortress and a prison; after many generations there will be a visitation of them.
The brick will melt and the wall will fall, because the Lord will reign in Zion and in Jerusalem and will be glorified before the elders.
Lord my God, I will glorify Thee and sing Thy name, because Thou hast done wondrous things, an ancient, true plan. May it be so, Lord!
For Thou hast made cities a mound, fortified cities so that their foundations fall. The city of the ungodly will certainly never be rebuilt.
Therefore the poor people will bless Thee, and cities of wronged people will bless Thee.
For Thou didst become a helper to every lowly city and a shelter to those discouraged by need. Thou wilt rescue them from evil people, a shelter for the thirsty and a breath for wronged people.
They will bless Thee like fainthearted people thirsting in Zion because of ungodly people, to whom Thou didst hand us over.
The Lord Sabaoth will act for all the nations upon this mountain. They will drink gladness, drink wine and anoint themselves with perfume.
On this mountain, hand all these things over to the nations, for this plan concerns all the nations.
Death swallowed, having prevailed; and again God removed every tear from every face. He removed the people’s reproach from all the earth, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken.
On that day they will say, “Behold, our God, in whom we hoped and exulted; and we will rejoice in our salvation.”
For God will give rest upon this mountain, and Moab’s land will be trampled as people tread a threshing floor with wagons,
and he will release his hands, just as he himself brought low for destruction; he will bring low his insolence over what he laid his hands on,
and he will bring low the height of your wall’s refuge, and it will descend to the ground.
On that day they will sing this song in Judah’s land, saying, “Behold, a fortified city! He will make our salvation a wall and an encircling wall.
Open the gates; let a people enter, keeping righteousness and keeping truth,
holding fast to truth and keeping peace. For in Thee
they hoped, Lord, for ever, the great, everlasting God,
Thou who didst humble and bring down those dwelling on high. Thou wilt cast down fortified cities and bring them to the ground,
and the feet of the meek and lowly will trample them.
The way of the devout became straight, and the way of the devout is prepared.
For the Lord’s way is judgment. We hoped in Thy name and in the remembrance
which our soul desires. From night my spirit rises early toward Thee, God, because Thine ordinances are light upon the earth. Learn righteousness, you dwelling upon the earth!
For the ungodly has ceased; he will certainly not learn righteousness upon the earth or practice truth. Let the ungodly be removed, so that he may not see the Lord’s glory.
Lord, Thine arm is high, and they did not know; when they know, they will be ashamed. Zeal will seize an undisciplined people, and now fire will consume the opponents.
Lord our God, give us peace, for Thou hast repaid everything to us.
Lord our God, acquire us! Lord, we know no other besides Thee; we name Thy name.
The dead will certainly not see life, nor will physicians ever raise them. Therefore Thou didst bring calamity, destroy and remove every male of theirs.
Add evils to them, Lord; add evils to all the earth’s glorious people!
Lord, in affliction I remembered Thee; in slight affliction Thy discipline was for us.
Like a woman in labor nearing childbirth and crying out in her pang, so we became toward Thy beloved because of fear of Thee, Lord.
We conceived, labored and gave birth; we produced the spirit of Thy salvation upon the earth, but those dwelling upon the earth will fall.
The dead will rise, those in the tombs will be awakened, and those in the earth will rejoice, for the dew from Thee is healing to them; but the earth of the ungodly will fall.”
Go, My people, enter your inner rooms, shut your door, hide for a little, a very little while, until the Lord’s wrath passes.
For behold, the Lord brings wrath from the holy place upon those dwelling on the earth. The earth will uncover its blood and will not cover those killed.
On that day God will bring the holy, great and strong sword against the dragon, the fleeing serpent, against the dragon, the crooked serpent, and will kill the dragon.
On that day, a beautiful vineyard; a desire to lead a song against her.
“I am a strong city, a besieged city; in vain I will water her, for she will be captured by night, and by day the wall will fall.

There is none who has not seized her. Who will set me to guard stubble in a field? Because of this hostility I rejected her.” Therefore, for this reason the Lord God has done everything He commanded. “I have been burned!”
the residents in her will cry. “Let us make peace with Him; let us make peace.”
Those coming, Jacob’s children—Israel will sprout and flower, and the inhabited world will be filled with his fruit.
Surely he will not be struck just as he himself struck, and be killed just as he himself killed?
Fighting and reproaching, he will send them away. Wast Thou not the One planning with a harsh spirit to destroy them with a spirit of wrath?

Therefore Jacob’s lawlessness will be removed, and this is his blessing: when I remove his sin, when they make all altar stones cut down like fine dust. Their trees will certainly not remain, and their idols will be cut down like a forest far away.
The inhabited flock will be released like an abandoned flock; it will be pasture for a long time, and there they will rest.

After a time there will be nothing green in her because it has dried. Women coming from a spectacle, come! For this is a people without understanding; therefore their Maker will certainly not pity them, nor will the One who formed them ever have mercy.
On that day the Lord will fence off from the River’s canal to Rhinocorura; but you, gather Israel’s sons one by one.
On that day they will sound the great trumpet. Those lost in the Assyrians’ country and those lost in Egypt will come and bow to the Lord upon the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

units.text: Why are we also in danger every hour?
I die daily, brothers—I affirm it by my boasting in you, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
If in a merely human way I fought with beasts in Ephesus, what benefit is there for me? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good habits.”
Sober up as you ought and do not sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I speak to your shame.
in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
But when this corruptible puts on incorruption and this mortal puts on immortality, then the written saying will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
“Where, death, is your victory? Where, death, is your sting?”
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
The Lord said to Samuel, “Behold, I am carrying out My words in Israel, so that both ears of everyone who hears them will resound.
On that day I will raise against Eli everything I have spoken concerning his house. I will begin and bring it to completion.
I have told him that I am taking vengeance on his house for ever for his sons’ wrongdoings, because his sons were reviling God, and even so he did not admonish them.
I swore concerning Eli’s house: the wrongdoing of Eli’s house shall never be expiated by incense or sacrifices.”
Samuel lay until morning, rose early in the morning, and opened the doors of the Lord’s house. Samuel was afraid to report the vision to Eli.
Eli said to Samuel, “Samuel, child.” He said, “Here I am.”
After these events and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came. He came against Judah, camped against the walled cities, and said he would seize them beforehand.
“Thus says Sennacherib king of the Assyrians: On what have you placed your trust, sitting within the siege in Jerusalem?
Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had arrived and that his face was set to wage war against Jerusalem.
and cities for the produce of grain, oil, and wine, mangers for every animal, and folds for the flocks,
and cities that he built for himself, and a great stock of sheep and cattle, because the Lord gave him exceedingly many possessions.
He consulted with his elders and mighty men about blocking the waters of the springs outside the city, and they joined in strengthening him.
Hezekiah himself blocked the upper outlet of the water of Gihon and directed the waters downward toward the southwest of the City of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

And so, concerning the ambassadors of the rulers from Babylon sent to him to learn from him about the wonder that had happened upon the land, the Lord left him to test him, to know what was in his heart.
The rest of Hezekiah’s deeds and his mercy are written in the prophecy of Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet and in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
He gathered a great crowd and blocked the waters of the springs and the river that divided the city, saying, “Let the king of Assyria not come and find abundant water and gain strength.”
Hezekiah grew strong and built the entire demolished wall and towers, and outside another defensive wall. He strengthened the retaining work of the City of David and prepared many weapons.
He appointed commanders of war over the people, and they gathered to him in the square at the gate of the ravine. He spoke to their hearts, saying,
“Be strong and act courageously. Do not be terrified before the king of Assyria or before the entire nation with him, because more are with us than with him.
With him are arms of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God, to save and to fight our war.” The people took courage from the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

After these things, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians sent his servants against Jerusalem; he himself was at Lachish, with all the army with him. He sent to Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah in Jerusalem, saying,
King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians. He saw the altar in Damascus, and King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest the altar’s likeness and design for all its construction.
Uriah the priest built the altar in accordance with everything King Ahaz sent from Damascus.
Then Raasson king of Syria and Phakee son of Romelias, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem for war. They besieged Ahaz but could not wage the battle successfully.
At that time Raasson king of Syria restored Ailath to Syria and expelled the Judeans from Ailath. Idumeans came to Ailath and lived there to this day.

Ahaz sent messengers to Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians, saying, ‘I am your slave and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising against me.’
Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the treasuries of the Lord’s house and the king’s house, and sent gifts to the king.
The king of the Assyrians listened to him. The king of the Assyrians went up against Damascus, captured it, deported it, and put Raasson to death.
Salamanasar king of the Assyrians went up against him. Hoshea became his slave and paid him manaa.

The king of the Assyrians found wrongdoing in Hoshea, because he had sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt and had not brought manaa to the king of the Assyrians in that year. The king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in prison.
The king of the Assyrians went up through the whole land, went up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
In Hoshea’s ninth year the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians. He settled them in Alae and Abor, rivers of Gozan, and Ore of the Medes.
This happened because the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up from Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
They walked in the ordinances of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites; and Israel’s kings, all who acted so,
At that time Hezekiah cut apart the doors of the Lord’s sanctuary and the fixed supports which Hezekiah king of Judah had gilded, and gave them to the king of the Assyrians.

The king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan, Raphis, and Rhapsakes from Lachish to King Hezekiah against Jerusalem with a great force. They went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road of the Fuller’s Field.
They called to Hezekiah. Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joash son of Asaph the recorder went out to him.
Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Tell Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you trust?
You said—only words of lips!—“Counsel and strength for war.” Now then, in whom do you trust, that you have broken with me?
By the road on which he came he shall return; he shall not enter this city, says the Lord.
I shall shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.’
By night the Lord’s angel went out and struck one hundred eighty-five thousand in the Assyrians’ camp. When they rose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead bodies.
Sennacherib king of the Assyrians departed, went away, returned, and lived in Nineveh.
As he was bowing down in the house of Neserach his god, his sons Adramelech and Sarasar struck him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Asordan became king in his place.

The king pulled down the altars on the roof of Ahaz’s upper chamber which Judah’s kings had made, and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the Lord’s house. He tore them down from there and threw their dust into the Kidron torrent.

The king defiled the house facing Jerusalem, to the right of Mount Mosoath, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Astarte, the Sidonians’ offensive thing, for Chamos, Moab’s offensive thing, and for Molchol, the Ammonites’ abomination.
He shattered the pillars, destroyed the groves, and filled their sites with human bones.

Moreover, he tore down the altar at Bethel, the high place Jeroboam son of Nabat had made, who caused Israel to sin—both that altar and the high place. He shattered its stones, reduced it to dust, and burned the grove.

Josiah turned aside and saw the tombs there in the city. He sent and took the bones from the tombs, burned them on the altar, and defiled it, according to the Lord’s word which the man of God spoke while Jeroboam stood at the festival beside the altar. Turning, he lifted his eyes toward the tomb of the man of God who had spoken these words.
He said, ‘What is that rocky marker I see?’ The city’s men told him, ‘It is the man of God who came out of Judah and proclaimed these words which he proclaimed against Bethel’s altar.’
In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came with all his force against Jerusalem. He camped against it and built an enclosing wall against it all around.
The city remained under siege until King Sedekias’s eleventh year.

Babylon, which is called glorious by the king of the Chaldeans, will be as when God overturned Sodom and Gomorrah.
She will not be inhabited for everlasting time, nor will people ever enter her through many generations. Arabs will certainly not pass through her, and shepherds will certainly not rest in her.
Wild beasts will rest there, and the houses fill with sound; sirens will rest there, and demons dance there.
Donkey-centaurs will dwell there, and hedgehogs make nests in their houses. It comes quickly and will not delay.
Wail, for the Lord’s day is near, and shattering will come from God.
Therefore every hand will slacken, and every human soul grow cowardly;
the envoys will be troubled, and labor pains will hold them like those of a woman giving birth. They will lament to one another and be distraught, and change their face as to flame.
For behold, the Lord’s incurable day comes, of wrath and anger, to make the whole inhabited world deserted and destroy its sinners from it.
It will turn to your shame, because Moab labored at the altars and will enter her handmade objects to pray; it will certainly not be able to rescue him.
This is the utterance the Lord spoke against Moab, whenever He spoke it.
Now I say, “In three years, years of a hired worker, Moab’s glory will be dishonored with all its abundant wealth, and a very small, unhonored remnant will be left.”
Moab’s fugitives will sojourn with you; they will be a shelter for you from the pursuer, because your alliance was removed, and the ruler trampling the earth perished.
A throne will be set right with mercy, and one will sit upon it with truth in David’s tent, judging, seeking judgment and hastening righteousness.
We heard Moab’s insolence—exceedingly insolent. You raised up your arrogance. Your divination is not so,
not so. Moab will wail, for all in Moab’s country will wail. You will ponder for Deseth’s residents and not be ashamed.

Hesebon’s plains will mourn, and Sebama’s vine. You who devour the nations, trample her vineyards as far as Iazer; you will certainly not reach them. Wander in the wilderness! Those sent out were abandoned, for they crossed the wilderness.
Therefore I will weep like Iazer’s weeping for Sebama’s vine. He felled your trees, Hesebon and Eleale, because I will trample upon your grain harvest and vintage, and all will fall.
The utterance against Damascus. Behold, Damascus will be removed from the cities and become a ruin,
because you abandoned God your Savior and did not remember the Lord your Helper. Therefore you will plant a faithless planting and faithless seed;
on the day you plant, you will wander. In the morning, if you sow, it will blossom for harvest on whatever day you allot, and like a human father you will allot to your sons.
Woe, the multitude of many nations! Like a surging sea, so you will be troubled, and the back of many nations will roar like water.

Many nations are like abundant water, like much water violently rushing down. He will drive him away and pursue him far off, like chaff-dust when people winnow before wind, and like wheel-dust carried by a squall.
Toward evening there will be mourning; before morning it will be gone. This is the portion of those who plundered you, an inheritance for those who took possession of you.
abandoned for everlasting time, a bed and resting place for flocks, with no one pursuing.

There will no longer be a stronghold for Ephraim to flee to, nor a kingdom in Damascus, and the Syrians’ remainder will perish; for you are no better than Israel’s sons and their glory. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.
On that day Jacob’s glory will fail, and the fat parts of his glory will be shaken.
It will be as when someone gathers a standing harvest and reaps seed from the ears in his arm, as when someone gathers an ear in a firm ravine,
and a stalk is left in it, or like olive berries, two or three on a lofty top, or four or five left on their branches. Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God.
On that day a person will trust in the One who made him, and his eyes will look toward Israel’s Holy One,
and they will certainly not trust the altars or their hands’ works, which their fingers made, nor look at their trees or abominations.
On that day your cities will be abandoned as the Amorites and Hivites abandoned theirs before Israel’s sons, and they will be deserted,
Woe, wings of a land of ships, beyond Ethiopia’s rivers,

the one sending hostages by sea and papyrus letters over the water! For swift messengers will go to a lofty nation and a foreign and harsh people—who is beyond it?—a hopeless and trampled nation. Now the land’s rivers,
all are like an inhabited country; their country will be inhabited as when a signal is raised from a mountain, and it will be audible like a trumpet’s voice.
For thus the Lord said to me, “There will be security in My city, like the light of midday heat, and it will be like a dew cloud on a harvest day.”

Before harvest, when the bloom is complete and the unripe grape blossoms as its flower forms unripe fruit, He will remove the small grape clusters with sickles, remove the vine branches and cut them down,
and leave them together for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts. Heaven’s birds will gather upon them, and all the earth’s wild beasts will come upon him.

At that time gifts will be brought to the Lord Sabaoth from a people afflicted and plucked, and from a great people from now on and for everlasting time—a hoping and trampled nation, which is in a part of its country’s river—to the place where the Lord Sabaoth’s name was called, Mount Zion.
A vision of Egypt. Behold, the Lord sits upon a light cloud and will come into Egypt; Egypt’s handmade objects will be shaken before Him, and their heart overcome within them.
and those warping them will be in pain, and all who make beer will be grieved and suffer in their souls.
Tanis’s rulers will be fools; the king’s wise counselors—their counsel will become foolish. How will you say to the king, “We are sons of the discerning, sons of kings from the beginning”?
Where are your wise men now? Let them announce to you and say what the Lord Sabaoth has counseled against Egypt.
Tanis’s rulers failed, and Memphis’s rulers were exalted; they will lead Egypt astray tribe by tribe.
For the Lord mixed for them a spirit of wandering; they led Egypt astray in all their works, as someone wanders while drunk and vomiting.
There will be no work for the Egyptians that will produce a head and tail, a beginning and end.
On that day the Egyptians will be like women in fear and trembling before the Lord Sabaoth’s hand, which He Himself will bring upon them.
The Judeans’ country will become a terror to the Egyptians; whenever anyone names her to them, they will fear because of the counsel the Lord has counseled against her.
On that day five cities in Egypt will speak the Canaanite language and swear by the Lord’s name. One city will be called City-Asedek.
On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the Egyptians’ country and a pillar to the Lord by its border,
Egyptians will be roused against Egyptians; each will fight his brother and each his neighbor, city against city and district against district.

and it will be an everlasting sign to the Lord in Egypt’s country, because they will cry to the Lord on account of their oppressors. The Lord will send them a man who will save them; judging, he will save them.
The Lord will be known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day. They will make sacrifices, vow vows to the Lord and pay them.
The Lord will strike the Egyptians with a great blow and heal them with healing. They will turn back to the Lord, and He will listen to them and heal them.
On that day there will be a road from Egypt toward the Assyrians. Assyrians will enter Egypt, and Egyptians go toward the Assyrians, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians.
On that day Israel will be third among the Assyrians and Egyptians, blessed upon the earth,
which the Lord Sabaoth blessed, saying, “Blessed be My people in Egypt and among the Assyrians, and My inheritance Israel.”
The Egyptians’ spirit will be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel. They will inquire of their gods, their statues, those speaking from the earth and the belly-speakers.
I will hand Egypt into the hands of harsh human masters, and harsh kings will rule them. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.
The Egyptians will drink water beside the sea, but the river will fail and dry up.
Rivers and the river’s canals will fail, and every gathering of water dry up, in every marsh of reed and papyrus,
and all the green marsh growth around the river and everything sown by the river will dry up, destroyed by wind.
Fishermen will groan, and all casting a hook into the river will groan; those casting seines and those using casting nets will mourn.
Shame will seize those working split flax and those working fine linen,
The vision that Isaiah son of Amos saw, which he saw against Judea and against Jerusalem during the reign of Oziah, Joatham, Achaz and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judea.
Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.
An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”
Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless sons! You abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.
Why should you be struck again as you add lawlessness? Every head is in pain, and every heart in grief.
From feet to head: for neither a wound nor a bruise nor an inflamed blow is there a poultice to apply, nor oil nor bandages.
In the year Tanathan entered Azotus, when he was sent by Arna king of the Assyrians and fought Azotus and seized it,
then the Lord spoke to Isaiah, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and untie the sandals on your feet.” He did so, going naked and without sandals.
The Lord said, “As Isaiah My servant has gone naked and without sandals for three years, there will be signs and wonders for the Egyptians and Ethiopians;
for thus the king of the Assyrians will lead Egypt’s and the Ethiopians’ captivity, young men and elders, naked and without sandals, exposed as Egypt’s shame.
The Egyptians will be ashamed in defeat because of the Ethiopians, in whom the Egyptians had trusted, for they were their glory.
Those dwelling on this island will say, ‘Behold, we had trusted that we could flee to them for help, but they could not be saved from the king of the Assyrians. How, then, shall we be saved?’”
The vision of the wilderness. As a squall might pass through a wilderness, coming from a wilderness, from a land—a fearsome
Hear, you who remain and suffer; hear what I heard from the Lord Sabaoth. Israel’s God announced it to us.
The vision of Idumea. One calls to me from Seir: “Guard the battlements.”
“I watch morning and night. If you seek, seek, and dwell beside me;
in the wood you will sleep at evening, on Daidan’s road.”
Bring water to meet the thirsty, you dwelling in Thaiman’s country; meet the fugitives with loaves,
because of the multitude of those fleeing, the multitude of those wandering, the multitude of the sword, the multitude of ready arrows, and the multitude of those fallen in war.
For thus the Lord said to me: “Yet one year, like a hired worker’s year, and the glory of Kedar’s sons will fail,
and the remaining arrows of Kedar’s strong sons will be few, because the Lord, Israel’s God, has spoken.”

and harsh vision was announced to me. The faithless person deals faithlessly, and the lawless person acts lawlessly. The Elamites are against me, and Persian envoys come against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.
Therefore my loins filled with weakness, and labor pains seized me like a woman giving birth. I did wrong by not hearing; I strove not to see.
My heart wanders, and lawlessness submerges me; my soul stands in fear.
Prepare the table; drink, eat! Rise, rulers; prepare shields!
For thus the Lord said to me: “Go, station a watcher for yourself, and report whatever you see.
I saw mounted riders, two horsemen, a donkey rider and a camel rider. Listen with great attention,
and call Uriah to the Lord’s watchtower.” He said, “I stood continually by day, and at the camp I stood all night,
and behold, he himself comes, a rider of a two-horse team.” He answered and said, “Babylon has fallen, and all her statues and handmade objects were shattered to the ground.”
The utterance of Zion’s ravine. What happened to you now, that you all went up to the roofs,
and that Jerusalem’s houses had been pulled down to fortify the city’s wall.
You provided water for yourselves between the two walls, inside the old pool, and did not look to the One who made her from the beginning or see the One who founded her.
The Lord Sabaoth called on that day for weeping, lamentation, shaving and putting on sackcloth,
but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
These things are revealed in the Lord Sabaoth’s ears: “This sin will not be forgiven you until you die.”
Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: “Go into the chamber to Somnas the treasurer, and say to him,
What are you doing here, and what do you have here, that you quarried yourself a memorial here, made yourself a memorial on high and inscribed yourself a dwelling in rock?
Behold, the Lord Sabaoth will cast out and crush a man and remove your robe,
and your glorious crown, and throw you into a great and immeasurable country. There you will die; He will make your fine chariot dishonored and your ruler’s house a trampling place,
and you will be removed from your stewardship and your standing.
the futile roofs? The city was filled with people crying out. Your wounded were not wounded by a sword, nor did your dead die in war.
On that day I will call My servant Eliakim, son of Chelkias,
clothe him in your robe, give him your crown, and put the power and your stewardship in his hands. He will be like a father to those dwelling in Jerusalem and those dwelling in Judah.
I will give him David’s glory, and he will rule, with no one contradicting.
I will establish him as a ruler in a trustworthy place, and he will become a throne of glory for his father’s house.
Every glorious person in his father’s house, from small to great, will trust in him, and they will hang upon him.
On that day—thus says the Lord Sabaoth—the person established in a trustworthy place will be shaken and fall, and the glory upon him will be removed, because the Lord has spoken.”
All your rulers have fled; those captured are harshly bound, and the strong among you have fled far away.
Therefore I said, “Leave me; I will weep bitterly. Do not insist on comforting me over the shattering of the daughter of my race.”
For there is a day of disturbance, destruction, trampling and wandering from the Lord Sabaoth in Zion’s ravine. They wander from small to great; they wander upon the mountains.
The Elamites took quivers—mounted men upon horses and an assembled battle line.
Your chosen ravines will be filled with chariots, and the horsemen will block your gates,
and they will uncover Judah’s gates and look on that day into the city’s choice houses,
and uncover the hidden things of the houses in David’s citadel. They saw that they were many and that the old pool’s water had been diverted into the city,
The vision of Tyre. Wail, ships of Carthage, because she has perished, and they no longer come from the Kitians’ land; she has been led captive.
Work your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage.
Your hand no longer has strength at sea, the hand that provoked kings. The Lord Sabaoth commanded concerning Canaan, to destroy her strength.
They will say, “You shall no longer continue in insolence and in wronging Sidon’s daughter.” Even if you go to the Kitians, there too you will have no rest,
and into the Chaldeans’ land: this too has been devastated by the Assyrians. There too you will have no rest, because her wall has fallen.
Wail, ships of Carthage, because your fortress has perished!
On that day Tyre will be left for seventy years, like a king’s time, like a person’s time. After seventy years, Tyre will be like a prostitute’s song:
“Take a lyre, wander through cities, forgotten prostitute! Play the lyre well, sing much, so that you may be remembered.”
After seventy years God will visit Tyre, and she will again be restored to her former state and become a trading center for all the inhabited world’s kingdoms.

Her trade and her wage will be holy to the Lord. It will not be collected for them; instead, all her trade will be for those dwelling before the Lord, to eat and drink and be filled, as a contribution, a memorial before the Lord.
Whom have the island-dwelling traders of Phoenicia become like, crossing the sea
upon much water, seed of traders? Like a harvest being brought in are the nations’ traders.
“Be ashamed, Sidon,” said the sea; and the sea’s strength said, “I did not labor or give birth or rear young men or raise maidens.”
When it becomes known to Egypt, pain will seize them concerning Tyre.
Go away to Carthage! Wail, residents of this island!
Was this not your insolence from the beginning, before she was handed over?
Who planned these things against Tyre? Is she weaker, or has she no strength? Her merchants are glorious, rulers of the earth.
The Lord Sabaoth planned it, to dissolve all the insolence of the glorious and dishonor everything glorious upon the earth.
Behold, the Lord is destroying the inhabited world; He will make it desolate, uncover its face and scatter those dwelling in it.
Every city was deserted; he will shut a house so that none may enter.
Wail over wine everywhere! All the earth’s gladness has ceased.
Cities will be left deserted, and abandoned houses will perish.
All these things will happen on the earth, among the nations: as when someone gleans an olive tree, so they will glean them, even when the grape harvest has ceased.
These will cry aloud, and those left upon the earth will rejoice together with the Lord’s glory. The sea’s water will be troubled;
therefore the Lord’s glory will be in the sea’s islands; the Lord’s name will be glorious—O Lord, Israel’s God!
From the earth’s wings we heard wonders: “Hope for the devout!” And they will say, “Woe to those who reject, those who reject the law!”
Fear, pit and trap are upon you who dwell on the earth!
Whoever flees the fear will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught by the trap, because windows from heaven have opened and the earth’s foundations will be shaken.
The earth will be utterly agitated, and the earth will be utterly at a loss;

The people will be like the priest, the slave like the master, the maidservant like the mistress; the buyer will be like the seller, the lender like the borrower, and the debtor like the one to whom he owes a debt.
The earth has tilted and will be shaken like a fruit-watcher’s shelter, like someone drunk and hungover. It will fall and will never be able to rise, for lawlessness has prevailed upon it.
God will bring His hand against heaven’s array and against the earth’s kings.
They will gather and shut them into a fortress and a prison; after many generations there will be a visitation of them.
The brick will melt and the wall will fall, because the Lord will reign in Zion and in Jerusalem and will be glorified before the elders.
The earth will be utterly destroyed, and the earth utterly plundered, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken these things.
The earth mourned, the inhabited world was destroyed, and the earth’s high ones mourned.
The earth acted lawlessly because of those dwelling in it, because they transgressed the law and changed the ordinances, an everlasting covenant.
Therefore a curse will consume the earth, because those dwelling in it sinned. Therefore those dwelling on the earth will be poor, and few people will be left.
Wine will mourn, the vine will mourn, and all who gladden the soul will groan.
The joy of tambourines has ceased; the impudence and wealth of the ungodly have ceased; the lyre’s sound has ceased.
They were ashamed and did not drink wine; sikera became bitter to those drinking it.
Lord my God, I will glorify Thee and sing Thy name, because Thou hast done wondrous things, an ancient, true plan. May it be so, Lord!
For God will give rest upon this mountain, and Moab’s land will be trampled as people tread a threshing floor with wagons,
and he will release his hands, just as he himself brought low for destruction; he will bring low his insolence over what he laid his hands on,
and he will bring low the height of your wall’s refuge, and it will descend to the ground.
For Thou hast made cities a mound, fortified cities so that their foundations fall. The city of the ungodly will certainly never be rebuilt.
Therefore the poor people will bless Thee, and cities of wronged people will bless Thee.
For Thou didst become a helper to every lowly city and a shelter to those discouraged by need. Thou wilt rescue them from evil people, a shelter for the thirsty and a breath for wronged people.
They will bless Thee like fainthearted people thirsting in Zion because of ungodly people, to whom Thou didst hand us over.
The Lord Sabaoth will act for all the nations upon this mountain. They will drink gladness, drink wine and anoint themselves with perfume.
On this mountain, hand all these things over to the nations, for this plan concerns all the nations.
Death swallowed, having prevailed; and again God removed every tear from every face. He removed the people’s reproach from all the earth, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken.
On that day they will say, “Behold, our God, in whom we hoped and exulted; and we will rejoice in our salvation.”
On that day they will sing this song in Judah’s land, saying, “Behold, a fortified city! He will make our salvation a wall and an encircling wall.
For the ungodly has ceased; he will certainly not learn righteousness upon the earth or practice truth. Let the ungodly be removed, so that he may not see the Lord’s glory.
Lord, Thine arm is high, and they did not know; when they know, they will be ashamed. Zeal will seize an undisciplined people, and now fire will consume the opponents.
Lord our God, give us peace, for Thou hast repaid everything to us.
Lord our God, acquire us! Lord, we know no other besides Thee; we name Thy name.
The dead will certainly not see life, nor will physicians ever raise them. Therefore Thou didst bring calamity, destroy and remove every male of theirs.
Add evils to them, Lord; add evils to all the earth’s glorious people!
Lord, in affliction I remembered Thee; in slight affliction Thy discipline was for us.
Like a woman in labor nearing childbirth and crying out in her pang, so we became toward Thy beloved because of fear of Thee, Lord.
We conceived, labored and gave birth; we produced the spirit of Thy salvation upon the earth, but those dwelling upon the earth will fall.
The dead will rise, those in the tombs will be awakened, and those in the earth will rejoice, for the dew from Thee is healing to them; but the earth of the ungodly will fall.”
Open the gates; let a people enter, keeping righteousness and keeping truth,
Go, My people, enter your inner rooms, shut your door, hide for a little, a very little while, until the Lord’s wrath passes.
For behold, the Lord brings wrath from the holy place upon those dwelling on the earth. The earth will uncover its blood and will not cover those killed.
holding fast to truth and keeping peace. For in Thee
they hoped, Lord, for ever, the great, everlasting God,
Thou who didst humble and bring down those dwelling on high. Thou wilt cast down fortified cities and bring them to the ground,
and the feet of the meek and lowly will trample them.
The way of the devout became straight, and the way of the devout is prepared.
For the Lord’s way is judgment. We hoped in Thy name and in the remembrance
which our soul desires. From night my spirit rises early toward Thee, God, because Thine ordinances are light upon the earth. Learn righteousness, you dwelling upon the earth!
On that day God will bring the holy, great and strong sword against the dragon, the fleeing serpent, against the dragon, the crooked serpent, and will kill the dragon.
The inhabited flock will be released like an abandoned flock; it will be pasture for a long time, and there they will rest.

After a time there will be nothing green in her because it has dried. Women coming from a spectacle, come! For this is a people without understanding; therefore their Maker will certainly not pity them, nor will the One who formed them ever have mercy.
On that day the Lord will fence off from the River’s canal to Rhinocorura; but you, gather Israel’s sons one by one.
On that day they will sound the great trumpet. Those lost in the Assyrians’ country and those lost in Egypt will come and bow to the Lord upon the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
On that day, a beautiful vineyard; a desire to lead a song against her.
“I am a strong city, a besieged city; in vain I will water her, for she will be captured by night, and by day the wall will fall.

There is none who has not seized her. Who will set me to guard stubble in a field? Because of this hostility I rejected her.” Therefore, for this reason the Lord God has done everything He commanded. “I have been burned!”
the residents in her will cry. “Let us make peace with Him; let us make peace.”
Those coming, Jacob’s children—Israel will sprout and flower, and the inhabited world will be filled with his fruit.
Surely he will not be struck just as he himself struck, and be killed just as he himself killed?
Fighting and reproaching, he will send them away. Wast Thou not the One planning with a harsh spirit to destroy them with a spirit of wrath?

Therefore Jacob’s lawlessness will be removed, and this is his blessing: when I remove his sin, when they make all altar stones cut down like fine dust. Their trees will certainly not remain, and their idols will be cut down like a forest far away.
Expect affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope, yet a little, yet a little,
On that day the Lord Sabaoth will be the crown of hope, woven of glory, for My people who remain;
they will be left with a spirit of judgment, for judgment and strength, as He prevents destruction.
For these have been led astray by wine and wandered because of sikera. Priest and prophet lost their senses because of wine, reeled from sikera’s intoxication and went astray. This is an apparition.
A curse will consume this counsel, for this counsel is for greed.
To whom did we announce evils, and to whom did we announce a message—you weaned from milk, torn from a breast?
This book will be given into the hands of a person who does not know how to read. Someone will say to him, “Read this,” and he will say, “I do not know how to read.”
The Lord said, “This people draws near Me; with their lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me. They revere Me in vain, teaching human commands and teachings.
Therefore, behold, I will proceed to remove this people; I will remove them, destroy the wise people’s wisdom and hide the discerning people’s understanding.”

Woe to those making deep counsel, but not through the Lord! Woe to those making counsel in secret! Their deeds will be in darkness, and they will say, “Who has seen us, and who will know us or what we do?”
Will you not be reckoned as the potter’s clay? Will the formed thing say to its former, “You did not form me,” or the work to its maker, “You did not make me intelligently”?
The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah son of Amos concerning Judea and Jerusalem.
And now enter the rocks and hide in the earth from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.
For the Lord’s eyes are high, but the human being is low; humanity’s height will be humbled, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
For the Lord Sabaoth has a day against every insolent and arrogant person, against everyone high and elevated; they will be humbled,
against every cedar of Lebanon among the high and elevated, and against every oak tree of Bashan,
against every mountain and every high hill,
against every high tower and every high wall,
against every ship of the sea and every beautiful display of ships.
Every human being will be humbled, humanity’s height will fall, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
They will hide away all the handmade things,
carrying them into caves, into clefts in the rocks and into holes in the earth, from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.
In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

He will judge between the nations and reprove a numerous people. They will beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will no longer take sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war.
And now, house of Jacob, come, let us walk by the Lord’s light!
For He abandoned His people, Israel’s house, because their country was filled, as from the beginning, with omens like the foreigners’ country, and many foreign children were born to them.
For their country was filled with silver and gold, and their treasures had no number; the land was filled with horses, and their chariots had no number.
The land was filled with abominations, the works of their hands, and they bowed before what their fingers made.
A human being bowed down, and a man was humbled; I will certainly not let them go.
“Woe, rebellious children,” thus says the Lord, “you made a plan not through Me and agreements not through My spirit, to add sins upon sins,
you who go down to Egypt, but they did not ask Me, to be helped by Pharaoh and sheltered by Egyptians.
For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.
For there are leaders in Tanis, evil messengers; they will labor in vain
toward a people that will not benefit them, neither for assistance nor for profit, but for shame and reproach.”

The vision of the four-footed creatures in the wilderness. In affliction and hardship, a lion and lion cub from there, asps and offspring of flying asps; they carried their wealth on donkeys and camels to a nation that will not benefit them with help, but with shame and reproach.
Egyptians will benefit you with futile and empty things. Announce to them, “This consolation of yours is futile.”
Woe to those going down to Egypt for help, trusting in horses and chariots because there are many, and in horses, a very great multitude, but not trusting Israel’s Holy One or seeking God!
He Himself, wise, brought evils upon them; His word will certainly not be set aside. He will rise against evil people’s houses and against their futile hope,
an Egyptian human being and not God, horses’ flesh, with no help. The Lord will bring His hand against them; the helpers will grow weary, and all will perish together.

For thus the Lord said to me: “As a lion or lion cub cries over prey it has caught and shouts over it until the mountains fill with its voice, and they are defeated and terrified by the greatness of its wrath, so the Lord Sabaoth will descend to march upon Mount Zion, upon her mountains.
Like flying birds, so the Lord will shield Jerusalem, rescue, preserve and save.”
For the Lord’s wrath is against all nations, and anger against their number, to destroy them and hand them over to slaughter.
Their wounded and dead will be thrown out; their odor will rise, and mountains will be soaked with their blood.
Heaven will roll up like a scroll, and all the stars will fall like leaves from a vine, like leaves falling from a fig tree.
My sword became drunk in heaven. Behold, it will descend upon Idumea and upon the people of destruction, with judgment.
The Lord’s sword was filled with blood, thickened with lambs’ fat and the fat of male goats and rams, for the Lord has a sacrifice in Bosor and a great slaughter in Idumea.
Sing a new hymn to the Lord—its beginning: “Glorify His name from the earth’s extremity, you who go down to the sea and sail it, islands and their inhabitants.”
Rejoice, wilderness and its villages, settlements and those inhabiting Kedar. Those inhabiting Petra will rejoice and cry out from the mountain tops.
They will give God glory and announce His praiseworthy deeds in the islands.
The Lord God of Powers will go out and crush war. He will rouse zeal and cry out mightily against His enemies.
“I was silent; surely I will not always be silent and hold back? I endured like a woman giving birth; I will astonish and dry up together.
I am the Lord God; this is My name. I will not give My glory to another or My praiseworthy deeds to carved images.
Behold, the things from the beginning have arrived, and new things I will announce; before they spring up, they were disclosed to you.”
Rejoice, heavens, because God had mercy on Israel! Sound trumpets, earth’s foundations! Cry out joy, mountains, hills and all their trees! For God redeemed Jacob, and Israel will be glorified.
Thus says the Lord who redeems you and forms you from the womb: “I am the Lord who completes all things. I stretched heaven alone and established the earth. Who else
will scatter the signs of spirit-mediums and divinations from the heart, turning the discerning backward and making their counsel foolish,

and establish His servant’s words and make His messengers’ counsel true? He says to Jerusalem, ‘You will be inhabited,’ and to Judea’s cities, ‘You will be rebuilt,’ and her deserted places will spring up;
He says to the abyss, ‘You will be desolate, and I will dry your rivers’;
announcing the last things beforehand, before they came to be—and together they were fulfilled. I said, ‘All My counsel will stand, and I will do everything I have planned,’
calling a bird from the east and from a distant land concerning what I have planned. I spoke and brought it about; I created and acted. I brought him and made his journey prosper.
Listen to Me, you who have lost heart, who are far from righteousness.
Remember these things and groan. Repent, you who have wandered astray; turn back in heart.
Remember the former things from eternity, for I am God, and there is none besides Me,
“Come down and sit on the ground, virgin daughter Babylon. Enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, for you will no longer be called tender and pampered.
Take a millstone and grind flour. Uncover your veil, expose your gray hair, pull up your garments to bare your lower legs, and cross rivers.
Your shame will be uncovered, and your reproaches will be visible. I will exact justice from you; I will certainly no longer hand it over to humans.”
The One who rescued you said—His name is the Lord Sabaoth, Israel’s Holy One—
“Sit stricken and enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will certainly no longer be called a kingdom’s strength.
If you had listened to My commands, your peace would have become like a river and your righteousness like a sea wave.
Your offspring would have become like sand, those born from your belly like the earth’s dust. Even now you will certainly not be destroyed, nor will your name perish before Me.”
Leave Babylon, fleeing from the Chaldeans. Announce a voice of rejoicing, and let this be heard; proclaim it to the earth’s extremity. Say, “The Lord rescued His slave Jacob.”
Even if they thirst, He will lead them through a wilderness and bring water out of a rock for them. A rock will split and water will flow, and My people will drink.
“There is no rejoicing for the ungodly,” says the Lord.
and those remaining in Zion and left in Jerusalem will be called holy, all those recorded for life in Jerusalem,
because the Lord will wash away the filth of Zion’s sons and daughters and thoroughly cleanse the blood from their midst, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

He will come, and it will be: a cloud will shade every place of Mount Zion and everything around her by day, and as of smoke and as of a light of fire burning by night; with all the glory it will be covered.
It will be shade from heat, shelter and concealment from harshness and rain.
‘I will not take vengeance on you for ever or always be angry with you. For spirit will go out from Me, and I made every breath.
Because of sin I grieved him a little, struck him, and turned My face away from him. He was grieved and went gloomily along his ways.
I have seen his ways, healed him, comforted him, and given him true comfort—
peace upon peace to those far away and those near. And the Lord said, ‘I will heal them.’
But the unjust will be tossed by waves in this way and will be unable to rest.
‘There is no rejoicing for the ungodly,’ said the Lord God.”

I did not choose this fast, or a day for a person to humble his life. Even if you bend your neck like a ring and spread sackcloth and ashes beneath you, you will not thereby call it an acceptable fast.

‘It is not such a fast that I chose,’ says the Lord. ‘Instead, loosen every bond of injustice, undo the strangling ties of coercive agreements, release the crushed, and tear up every unjust written contract.
Break your bread for the hungry and bring homeless poor people into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe him; do not overlook those belonging to your own family.
Then your light will break out early, and your healings quickly rise. Your righteousness will go ahead of you, and God’s glory will enfold you.
Then you will cry, and God will hear you. While you are still speaking He will say, “Behold, I am present.” If you remove from yourself a bond, finger-pointing, and a word of grumbling,
I will sing now to the beloved a song of the loved one for my vineyard. The beloved had a vineyard on a horn, in a fertile place.
I put a fence around it, surrounded it with a palisade, planted a Sorech vine, built a tower in its midst and dug a wine vat in it. I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now, man of Judah and residents of Jerusalem, judge My case and the matter of My vineyard.
What more shall I do for My vineyard that I did not do for it? For I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now I will announce to you what I will do to My vineyard: I will remove its fence, and it will be plundered; I will pull down its wall, and it will be trampled,
and I will abandon My vineyard. It will certainly not be pruned or dug, and thorns will rise in it as in fallow ground. I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.
For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.
Woe to those joining house to house and bringing field beside field, so that they may take something from their neighbor! Surely you will not dwell alone upon the earth?
For these things were heard in the ears of the Lord Sabaoth: “If many houses come to be, great and beautiful, they will become deserted, and no one will inhabit them.
Shine, shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the Lord’s glory has risen upon you.
You will suck the nations’ milk and eat kings’ wealth. You will know that I am the Lord who saves and delivers you, Israel’s God.
Instead of bronze I will bring you gold, instead of iron silver, instead of wood bronze, and instead of stones iron. I will appoint your rulers in peace and your overseers in righteousness.
Injustice will no longer be heard in your land, nor destruction and misery within your borders. Your walls will be called Salvation, and your gates Engraving.
The sun will not be your light by day, nor will the rising moon light your night. Instead, the Lord will be your everlasting light and God your glory.
Behold, darkness and gloom will cover earth over nations, but the Lord will appear upon you, and His glory will be seen over you.
For your sun will not set, and your moon will not fail. The Lord will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning will be fulfilled.
Kings will walk by your light, and nations by your radiance.
Lift your eyes around you and see your children gathered. Behold, all your sons have come from far away, and your daughters will be lifted upon shoulders.
Then you will see and fear and be astonished in heart, for the wealth of sea, nations, and peoples will turn toward you. There will come to you
herds of camels, and camels from Madiam and Gaipha will cover you. They will all come from Saba, bringing gold and carrying frankincense, and they will proclaim the Lord’s salvation as good news.
All Kedar’s sheep will gather to you, and Nabaioth’s rams will come to you. They will be offered acceptably upon My altar, and My house of prayer will be glorified.
Who are these flying like clouds and like doves with their young?
Islands waited for Me, and Tharsis ships among the first, to bring your children from far away, with silver and gold, because of the Lord’s holy name and because Israel’s Holy One is glorious.
For heaven will be new and earth new, and they will never remember former things, nor will those things enter their heart,
but they will find joy and exultation in it. For behold, I am making Jerusalem an exultation and My people joy.
I will exult over Jerusalem and rejoice over My people, and no sound of weeping or crying will ever again be heard in her.

There will never be one cut off prematurely there, nor an old man who fails to complete his time. For the young person will be a hundred years old, but the sinner who dies will be a hundred years old and accursed.
They will build houses and inhabit them themselves; they will plant vineyards and eat their own produce.
Rejoice, Jerusalem, and celebrate in her, all who love her! Rejoice with joy, all who mourn over her,
so that you may nurse and be filled from her comforting breast, so that, nursing fully, you may delight in the entrance of her glory.
A sound of shouting from the city, a sound from the temple, the sound of the Lord repaying recompense to His opponents!
Before the woman in labor gave birth, before the pain of labor came, she escaped and bore a male.
Who heard such a thing, and who has seen anything like it? Did a land labor in one day, or was a nation born all at once? For Zion labored and bore her children.
‘But I gave this expectation, and you did not remember Me,’ said the Lord. ‘Behold, did I not make the woman who gives birth and the barren woman?’ said God.

For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and they have closed their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn, and I will heal them.
And I said, How long, O Lord? And He said: Until cities lie waste, without inhabitants, and houses, without people, and the land is left desolate.
And after these things God will remove people far away; and those who remain will multiply upon the land.
And yet a tenth remains upon it; and again it will be for plunder, as a terebinth, and as an acorn when it falls from its husk.
And He said, Go, and say to this people: Hearing, you will hear and certainly not understand; and seeing, you will see and certainly not perceive.
He will say, “I will wait for God, who turned His face away from Jacob’s house, and I will put my trust in Him.”
Behold, I and the children God gave me—and it will be for signs and wonders in Israel’s house, from the Lord Sabaoth, who dwells on Mount Zion.

If they say to you, “Seek those who speak from the earth and the belly-speakers, the empty-talkers who speak from the belly,” should not a nation turn to its God? Why do they seek the dead concerning the living?
For He gave law for help, so that they might speak unlike this utterance, concerning which there are no gifts to give for it.
A harsh famine will come upon you; when you hunger, you will be grieved and speak evil of the ruler and the cult images, and they will look up toward heaven above,
Syria from the sun’s rising and the Greeks from the sun’s setting, who devour Israel with their whole mouth. For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
The people did not turn back until they were struck, and they did not seek the Lord.
The Lord removed from Israel head and tail, great and small, in one day,
the elder and those who show favoritism—this is the leadership—and the prophet teaching lawless things—this is the tail.
Those blessing this people will lead astray, and they lead astray in order to swallow them up.

Therefore God will not rejoice over their young men, and He will not pity their orphans or widows, because all are lawless and evil, and every mouth speaks unjust things. For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
Lawlessness will burn like fire and be consumed by fire like dry grass; it will burn in the forest’s thickets and consume together everything around the hills.
Through the fury of the Lord’s anger the whole earth has been burned, and the people will be as though burned by fire. A person will not pity his brother,
but will turn to the right because he will hunger, and eat from the left; a person eating the flesh of his own arm will certainly not be filled.
For Manasseh will eat from Ephraim, and Ephraim from Manasseh, because together they will besiege Judah. For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
And Pashhur son of Immer, the priest who had been appointed leader of the Lord’s house, heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.
And he struck him and put him into the trap, which was at the gate of the separated upper house that was in the Lord’s house.
And Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the trap, and Jeremiah said to him: The Lord has called your name not Pashhur but Migrant.

Because thus says the Lord: Behold, I am giving you to migration with all your friends. They will fall by their enemies’ sword, and your eyes will see. I will give you and all Judah into the hands of Babylon’s king, and they will deport them and cut them down with swords.
And I will give all this city’s strength, all its labors, and all the treasures of Judah’s king into his enemies’ hands, and they will bring them to Babylon.
And you and all who dwell in your house will go into captivity. In Babylon you will die and there be buried—you and all your friends to whom you prophesied false things.
Thou didst deceive me, Lord, and I was deceived. Thou tookest hold and didst prevail. I became a laughingstock; all day I continued being mocked.
Because I will laugh with my bitter word; I will call upon rejection and misery, because the Lord’s word became a reproach and a derision to me all day long.
And I will remove from them the sound of joy and delight, the sound of bridegroom and bride, the fragrance of ointment and the light of a lamp.
And all the land will become a ruin, and they will serve among the nations for seventy years.
