And when the seventy years are fulfilled, I will exact justice from that nation, says the Lord, and make them an everlasting ruin.
And I will bring upon that land all My words that I spoke against it, everything written in this book. What Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
What Jeremiah prophesied concerning the nations, Elam. At the beginning of King Zedekiah’s reign, this word came concerning Elam.
Thus says the Lord: Let Elam’s bow be shattered, the beginning of their dominion.
I will bring upon Elam four winds from heaven’s four ends and scatter them among all these winds. There will be no nation where Elam’s outcasts do not come.
I will terrify them before their enemies who seek their lives and bring calamities upon them according to the anger of My wrath. I will send My sword after them until they are consumed.

behold, I am sending and will take the clan from the north and bring them against this land, its inhabitants, and all the surrounding nations. I will lay them waste and make them a ruin, a hissing, and eternal reproach.
The Lord has brought forth His judgment. Come, let us announce in Zion the works of the Lord our God.
Prepare the arrows; fill the quivers. The Lord roused the spirit of the Medes’ king, for His anger against Babylon is to destroy her. This is the Lord’s vengeance, vengeance for His people.
Wounded men will fall in the Chaldeans’ land, and pierced men outside her.
For Israel and Judah have not been widowed of their God, of the Lord Almighty, because their land was filled with injustice from Israel’s holy ones.
Flee from Babylon’s midst; each of you save your life. Do not be cast away in her injustice, for her time of vengeance is from the Lord; He is repaying her recompense.
Babylon was a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, making the whole earth drunk. Nations drank her wine; therefore they were shaken.
Suddenly Babylon fell and was shattered. Lament her! Take resin for her corruption, if somehow she may be healed.
We treated Babylon, but she was not healed. Let us leave her; let each of us go to our own land, for her judgment reached heaven and rose to the stars.
Akkarioth was taken and the fortifications seized.
Moab will perish from being a multitude, for he magnified himself against the Lord.
Trap, fear, and pit are upon you, resident Moab.
One who flees from fear will fall into the pit, and one who climbs from the pit will be caught in the trap, for I will bring these things upon Moab in the year of her visitation.
The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still bound in the prison court:
Thus said the Lord: Again in this place, which you call deserted of people and animals, in Judah’s cities and outside Jerusalem, desolate because there are no people or animals, there will be heard
Thus said the Lord, who makes the earth and forms it to set it upright—the Lord is His name:
Cry out to Me and I will answer you. I will announce to you great, mighty things you have not known.
For thus said the Lord, Israel’s God, about this city’s houses and the houses of Judah’s king, torn down for siegeworks and defenses,
to fight the Chaldeans and fill the city with the dead bodies of people I struck in My anger and wrath. I turned My face from them because of all their wicked deeds.
I am bringing her the closing of wounds and a remedy. I will reveal to them that I listen, heal her, and make peace and faithfulness for them.
At that time they will say to this people and Jerusalem: A spirit of wandering in the wilderness; the daughter of My people’s way is not toward purity or holiness.
A spirit of filling will come to Me; but now I speak judgments against them.
Behold, he will come up like a cloud, and his chariots like a storm; his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, because we suffer misery!
Wash your heart clean of evil, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will the schemes of your troubles exist within you?
For the voice of one announcing will come from Dan, and trouble will be heard from Mount Ephraim.
Like those guarding a field they came against her all around, because you neglected Me, says the Lord.
Your ways and your practices have done these things to you. This is your evil: it is bitter; it has reached to your heart.
My belly, my belly, I am in pain, and the senses of my heart! My soul rages, my heart is torn; I will not be silent, because my soul heard the sound of a trumpet, a cry of war.
It calls out misery and crushing, because the whole land has suffered misery; suddenly the tent has suffered misery, and my tent coverings have been torn apart.
How long will I see people fleeing while hearing the sound of trumpets?
For the leaders of My people did not know Me; they are foolish sons and not discerning. They are wise at doing evil, but did not learn to do well.
I looked upon the earth, and behold, nothing; and into heaven, and its lights were not there.
I saw the mountains, and they were trembling, and all the hills were being shaken.
Thus says the Lord: The whole land will be a wilderness, but I will certainly not make a complete end.
For these things let the earth mourn and let heaven above grow dark, because I have spoken and will not change My mind; I have set Myself in motion and will not turn back from it.
At the sound of a horseman and a drawn bow the whole countryside withdrew; they entered caves and hid in groves and climbed onto the rocks. Every city was abandoned; no human dwells in them.

And you, what will you do if you put on scarlet and adorn yourself with golden ornaments, and if you paint your eyes with antimony? Your adornment is in vain; your lovers have rejected you; they seek your soul.

For I heard a voice like a woman in labor, your groaning like one giving birth for the first time, the voice of the daughter of Zion. She will grow faint and let her hands fall: Woe to me, because my soul fails over those killed!
Announce in Judah, and let it be heard in Jerusalem; say: Signal with a trumpet over the land, and cry loudly! Say: Gather, and let us enter the walled cities!
Take up and flee to Zion; hurry, do not stand still, for I am bringing evils from the north and great crushing.
A lion has gone up from his enclosure; destroying nations, he has set out and left his place to make the land a desolation, and cities will be demolished so that they are not inhabited.
And they built Topheth’s altar, which is in the ravine of the son of Hinnom, to burn up their sons and daughters in fire, which I did not command them and did not conceive in My heart.

Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say Topheth’s Altar or Ravine of the Son of Hinnom, but Ravine of the Slain; and they will bury in Topheth because there is no space.
And this people’s dead will be food for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts, and there will be no one to drive them off.

And I will stop the sound of those rejoicing and the sound of those glad, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, from Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s thoroughfares, because the whole land will become a desolation.
My belly is burned up from weeping, and a shadow lies upon my eyelids.
Yet there was nothing unjust in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
Earth, do not cover the blood of my flesh, and let there be no place for my cry!
Even now, behold, my witness is in the heavens, and the one who knows with me is in the highest places.
May my supplication reach the Lord, and may my eye drip tears before Him.
The pillars of heaven were spread out and were astonished at His rebuke.
By strength He calmed the sea, and by knowledge He wounded the great sea creature.
The bars of heaven have feared Him, and by a command He killed the rebellious dragon.
Behold, these are parts of His way, and we will hear a mere drop of speech concerning Him. But the strength of His thunder—who knows when He will act?”
because the plains have suffered. Let the earth mourn, because grain has suffered, wine has dried up, and oil has diminished.
The farmers have dried up. Lament, estates, over wheat and barley, because the harvest from the field has perished.
The vine has dried up and the fig trees have diminished; pomegranate, palm, apple tree and all the field’s trees have dried up, because human beings have put joy to shame.

Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.
Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service. Gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into your God’s house, and cry earnestly to the Lord,
“Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the Lord’s day is near, and it will come like suffering from suffering.”
Tell your children about these things, and let your children tell their children, and their children a further generation.
What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured; what the locust left, the bruchus locust devoured; what the bruchus locust left, the blight devoured.
Sober up, you drunkards, from their wine, and weep! Lament, all who drink wine to intoxication, because gladness and joy have been removed from your mouths.
For a nation has come up against My land, strong and uncountable. Its teeth are a lion’s teeth, and its grinding teeth a young lion’s.
It laid My vine waste and shattered My fig trees; searching, it searched it out and cast it away; it whitened its branches.
Lament to Me more than a bride wrapped in sackcloth for her first husband.
Sacrifice and drink offering have been removed from the Lord’s house. Mourn, priests who minister at the altar,
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,
Before them the earth will be thrown into turmoil and heaven shaken; the sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will sink their brightness.

The Lord will give His voice before His force, because His camp is very large, because the works of His words are strong. For the Lord’s day is great, great and very manifest; who will be sufficient for it?
“And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”
Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.
Who knows whether He will turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him, a sacrifice and drink offering for the Lord our God?
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service.

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist. Like dawn a numerous and strong people will be poured over the mountains. Its like has never existed, nor will another follow it through the years, for generations upon generations.
Assemble and enter, all surrounding nations, and gather there! Let the meek become a fighter!
Let all the nations be roused and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, because there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Send out sickles, because the vintage is at hand! Enter and tread, because the winepress is full; the vats overflow, because their evils have multiplied.
Sounds rang out in the Valley of Judgment, because the Lord’s day is near in the Valley of Judgment.
The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will sink their brightness.

Jesus knew that they wanted to ask Him, and said to them, “Are you seeking an answer among yourselves about this, because I said, ‘A little while, and you do not behold Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me’?
Amen, amen, I say to you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will become joy.

When a woman is giving birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come; but when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers the anguish because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
So you too now have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one takes your joy away from you.
And on that day you will ask Me nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask the Father anything, He will give it to you in My name.
Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be made full.
For just as the Father has life in Himself, so He also gave the Son to have life in Himself.
And He gave Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.
Do not marvel at this, because an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear His voice
and come out: those who did good things to a resurrection of life, but those who practiced base things to a resurrection of judgment.
I can do nothing from Myself. As I hear, I judge, and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of the One who sent Me.
If I bear witness concerning Myself, My testimony is not true.
We did this out of concern about this matter, saying, ‘Tomorrow your children might say to our children, “What do you have to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?
The Lord has made the Jordan a boundary between us and you, and you have no portion in the Lord.” Your sons would turn our sons away, so that they would not revere the Lord.’
We said that we should act in this way: build this altar, not for offerings and not for sacrifices,

but so that it may be a testimony between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform service to the Lord before Him with our offerings and our sacrifices and our sacrifices of well-being. Then your children shall not say to our children tomorrow, ‘You have no portion in the Lord.’

We said, ‘If ever they speak to us and to our generations tomorrow, they shall say, “Behold the likeness of the Lord’s altar which our fathers made, not for offerings or sacrifices, but as a testimony between you and us and between our sons.”’

May it never be that we turn away from the Lord in these present days, departing from the Lord by building an altar for offerings, salamin sacrifices, and a sacrifice of well-being apart from the Lord’s altar before His tent.”
When Phinehas the priest and all the leaders of the congregation of Israel with him heard the words spoken by the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, they were pleased.

And Phinehas the priest said to the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, “Today we know that the Lord is with us, for you have committed no offence before the Lord, and you have delivered the sons of Israel from the hand of the Lord.”
But the Lord your God was unwilling to destroy you. He blessed you abundantly, rescued you from their hands, and handed them over.

And you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. And the inhabitants of Jericho fought against you, the Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, Hittites, and Girgashites; and the Lord delivered them into your hands.
He sent the swarm of wasps before you, and it drove them out from before you, twelve kings of the Amorites, not by your sword or by your bow.
He gave you a land for which you did not labour, and cities which you did not build, and you were settled in them. You shall eat of vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant.
Now fear the Lord and serve Him with uprightness and righteousness. Remove the foreign gods your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.

But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: the gods of your fathers beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But I and my house will serve the Lord, for He is holy.”
Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and arrayed himself against Israel. He sent and called Balaam to curse you.
The Spirit of the Lord came upon him. He judged Israel and went out to war. The Lord gave Chousarsathom king of Syria into his hand, and his hand became strong against Chousarsathom.
The land was quiet for fifty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
The sons of Israel again did evil before the Lord. The Lord strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel because they had done evil before the Lord.
The sons of Israel did evil before the Lord, forgot the Lord their God, and served the Baalim and the groves.
And the Lord was greatly angered against Israel, and sold them into the hands of Chousarsathom king of Syria of the Rivers; and they served him eight years.
The sons of Israel cried out to the Lord. The Lord raised up a saviour for Israel and saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother. And he heard him.

After Israel was taken captive and Jerusalem laid waste, Jeremiah sat weeping and lamented this lament over Jerusalem, saying: How the city once full of peoples sat alone! She has become like a widow, she who was populous among the nations. A ruler among the regions has become subject to tribute.
From His height He sent fire; He brought it down into my bones. He spread a net for my feet; He turned me backward. He made me desolate, suffering pain all day long.
A watch was kept over my acts of ungodliness; they were intertwined in my hands and rose upon my neck. My strength weakened, because the Lord put pains into my hands; I will not be able to stand.
The Lord removed all my strong men from my midst. He called a time against me to crush my chosen men. The Lord trod a winepress for the virgin Daughter Judah; for these things I weep.
My eye brought down water, for the one who comforts me, who restores my life, is far from me. My sons have been destroyed, for the enemy has grown strong.
Zion spread out her hands; there is no one to comfort her. The Lord commanded concerning Jacob; around him are those who afflict him. Jerusalem has become like a woman sitting apart among them.
Jerusalem has sinned grievously; therefore she has come into upheaval. All who glorified her humbled her, for they saw her shame. She too groaned and turned backward.
Daughter Zion’s elders sat on the ground in silence. They put dust on their heads and girded themselves with sackcloth. They brought the leading virgins in Jerusalem down to the ground.
My eyes failed with tears; my heart was troubled. My glory was poured onto the ground at the shattering of the daughter of my people, as infant and nursing child failed in the city’s squares.
They said to their mothers, “Where are grain and wine?” They weakened like the wounded in the city’s squares, and their lives poured out into their mothers’ bosoms.
What can I testify to you, or what can I liken to you, Daughter Jerusalem? Who will save you and comfort you, virgin Daughter Zion? For the cup of your crushing has grown great; who will heal you?
Her gates were fixed in the earth; He destroyed and broke her bars. Her king and her rulers are among the nations. There is no law; even her prophets saw no vision from the Lord.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt while you were slaves. I shattered the bond of your yoke and led you with boldness.
But if you do not obey Me and do not do these ordinances of Mine,
but disobey them, and your soul is indignant at My judgments, so that you do not do all My commandments, so as to dissolve My covenant,
then I will do this to you: I will bring distress upon you, scab and jaundice that waste your eyes and melt away your life. You shall sow your seeds in vain, and your adversaries shall eat them.
And I will set My face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies. Those who hate you shall pursue you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
And if up to this point you do not obey Me, I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.

For look, the day of the Lord is coming, burning like an oven, and it will burn them. All the foreigners and all who practice lawlessness will be straw, and the coming day will ignite them,” says the Lord Almighty, “and neither root nor branch will remain from them.
But for you who fear My name, a sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in its wings; you will go out and leap like little calves released from bonds.
You will trample the lawless, because they will be ashes beneath your feet on the day that I am making,” says the Lord Almighty.
“And look, I am sending you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of the Lord’s great and manifest day,
who will restore a father’s heart toward a son and a person’s heart toward his neighbor, lest I come and strike the land utterly.”
Immediately after the affliction of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its brightness, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn; they will see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
He will send His angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather His chosen from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph came, who himself had also become Jesus’ disciple.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered it to be given.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
He laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut in the rock. Rolling a great stone to the tomb’s entrance, he went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.
On the next day, which was after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate,
When Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those following, “Truly I tell you, with no one in Israel have I found such faith.
I tell you that many will come from east and west and recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of the heavens,
but the sons of the kingdom will be cast into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.”
Jesus said to the centurion, “Go; as you have believed, let it happen for you.” And his servant was healed at that hour.
For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
Now many nations have gathered against you, saying, “We will rejoice over her, and our eyes will look upon Zion!”
But they did not know the Lord’s thought or understand His counsel, for He gathered them like sheaves of a threshing floor.

Rise and thresh them, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horns iron and your hooves bronze. With them you will melt down nations and grind many peoples fine; you will dedicate their multitude to the Lord and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.
Now the daughter of Ephraim will be fenced in with a barrier; he has set a constraint upon us. With a rod they will strike Israel’s tribes on the cheek.
For all the peoples will walk, each his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond.
“On that day,” says the Lord, “I will gather the crushed one, receive the expelled one and those I rejected.
I will make the crushed one a remnant and the rejected one a strong nation. The Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion from now and forever.
And you, squalid tower of the flock, daughter of Zion, to you it will come and enter—the former rule, a kingdom from Babylon for the daughter of Jerusalem.”
And now why have you experienced calamities? Did you have no king? Has your counsel perished, that birth pains have seized you like a woman giving birth?
You too will become drunk and be overlooked; you too will seek a place to stand away from enemies.
All your fortresses are fig trees having lookouts; if shaken, they will fall into the eater’s mouth.
Look, your people within you are like women! The gates of your land will open wide to your enemies, and fire will consume your bars.
Draw water for yourself for the siege, hold your fortresses firmly; step into mud, be trampled in straw, hold fast over the brick.
There fire will consume you; a sword will destroy you, devouring you like a locust, and you will become heavy like a crawling locust.
and everyone seeing you will spring away and say, “Miserable Nineveh! Who will lament her? Where shall I seek consolation for her?”
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons unto the priest, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.

And the priest shall prepare one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin in connection with the dead person, and shall consecrate his head on that day,

whereon he was consecrated unto the Lord for the days of the vow. And he shall bring a year-old lamb for a guilt offering; and the former days shall not be reckoned, for the head of his vow was defiled.
And this is the law of him who has vowed: on the day when he fulfils the days of his vow, he shall present his offering at the doors of the Tent of Testimony,
and he shall bring his gift unto the Lord: one unblemished year-old male lamb for whole burning, and one unblemished year-old ewe lamb for sin, and one unblemished ram for deliverance,
and a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, loaves prepared with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and their sacrifice and their drink offering.
And the priest shall present them before the Lord, and prepare his offering for sin and his whole burnt offering.
And he shall prepare the ram as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread; and the priest shall prepare its sacrifice and its drink offering.
And he who has vowed shall shave the head of his vow at the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and put the hair upon the fire which is under the sacrifice of deliverance.

And the priest shall take the boiled foreleg from the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them upon the hands of him who has vowed, after he has shaved the hair of his vow.
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a man or woman solemnly vows a vow of consecration unto the Lord, to be set apart

And the priest shall bring them as a presentation before the Lord. It shall be holy unto the priest, with the breast of presentation and the foreleg of the portion set apart; and afterward he who has vowed shall drink wine.

This is the law of him who vows unto the Lord, his gift unto the Lord concerning the vow, apart from whatever his hand may find, according to the extent of his vow which he vows under the law of consecration.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying: Thus you shall bless the sons of Israel, saying unto them (and they shall put My name upon the sons of Israel, and I, the Lord, will bless them):
The Lord bless you and keep you;
the Lord make His face shine upon you, and have mercy upon you;
the Lord lift up His face upon you, and give you peace.

from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins.
All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.
All the days of the vow of purification no razor shall come upon his head. Until the days which he vowed unto the Lord are fulfilled, he shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.
All the days of his vow unto the Lord he shall not enter where any dead person is.
For his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister, he shall not defile himself when they die; for the vow of his God is upon him, upon his head.
All the days of his vow he shall be holy unto the Lord.
But if anyone dies suddenly beside him, the head of his vow shall be defiled forthwith. He shall shave his head on the day when he is cleansed; on the seventh day it shall be shaved.
Rejoice in the Lord always. Again I will say: rejoice.
Let your gentleness be known to all people. The Lord is near.
Be anxious about nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever are honorable, whatever are just, whatever are pure, whatever are lovely, whatever are well spoken of, if there is any excellence and if there is any praise, consider these things.
Practice the things you learned and received and heard and saw in me; and the God of peace will be with you.
Righteousness cuts blameless paths straight, but impiety falls into injustice.
The righteousness of upright men rescues them, but lawless people are caught in their own destruction.
When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish, but the boast of the impious perishes.
The righteous escapes from the hunt, but the impious is handed over in his place.
In the mouth of the impious is a trap for citizens, but the discernment of the righteous has a good course.
Remove a crooked mouth from yourself and thrust unjust lips far away from you.
Let your eyes look straight, and let your eyelids incline toward righteous things.
Make straight tracks for your feet and direct your ways rightly.
Do not turn to the right or the left; turn your foot away from an evil way.
For God knows the ways on the right, but those on the left are perverted.
He Himself will make your tracks straight and advance your journeys in peace.
Those sitting in darkness and death’s shadow, fettered in poverty and iron,
He gathered them from the countries, from east and west and north and the sea.
They wandered in the wilderness, in a waterless place; they did not find a road to a city of habitation,
hungry and thirsty; their soul failed within them.
They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and He rescued them from their distresses,
and guided them into a straight way to travel to a city of habitation.
Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies and His wonders to the sons of men,
for He filled an empty soul and filled a hungry soul with good things.
I will not die, but live, and tell in full the works of the Lord.
The Lord disciplined me with discipline, and did not hand me over to death.
Open for me the gates of righteousness; entering through them, I will give thanks to the Lord.
This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous will enter through it.
I will thank Thee, for Thou heardest me and becamest my salvation.
The stone the builders rejected— this has become the head of the corner.
This has come from the Lord, and is marvelous in our eyes.
This is the day the Lord has made; let us exult and be glad in it.
O Lord, save now! O Lord, prosper us now!
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord. We have blessed you from the house of the Lord.
The Lord is God, and He has shone upon us. Arrange a festival among the thickly covering boughs, up to the horns of the altar.
Thou art my God, and I will thank Thee; Thou art my God, and I will exalt Thee. I will thank Thee, for Thou heardest me and becamest my salvation.
Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy is for ever.
I was prepared and was not troubled to keep Thy commandments.
Sinners’ cords entangled me, and I did not forget Thy law.
At midnight I would rise to give thanks unto Thee for Thy righteous judgments.
I am a companion of all who fear Thee and of those who keep Thy commandments.
The earth is full of Thy mercy, Lord; teach me Thine ordinances.
Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all Canaan’s kingdoms.
He gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel His people.
Lord, Thy name is for ever; Lord, Thy memorial is from generation to generation.
For the Lord will judge His people and be comforted concerning His slaves.
The nations’ idols are silver and gold, works of human hands.
They have a mouth but will not speak; they have eyes but will not see.
And He bent heaven and came down, and gloom was beneath His feet.
And He mounted cherubim and flew; He flew on the wings of winds.
And He made darkness His hiding place; His tent was around Him, dark water in clouds of the air.
From the far-shining radiance before Him, the clouds passed— hail and coals of fire.
And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave His voice.
And the earth was shaken and began to tremble; the foundations of the mountains were troubled and shaken because God was angry with them.
Smoke rose in His anger, and fire from His face set things ablaze; coals were kindled from Him.
When he burned Mesopotamia of Syria and Syria Zobah, and Joab returned and struck the Valley of Salt—twelve thousand.
God, Thou didst reject us and pull us down; Thou wast angry and hadst compassion on us.
Thou didst shake the earth and trouble it; heal its fractures, for it was shaken.
Thou didst show Thy people hard things; Thou madest us drink wine of stupor.
Thou gavest those who fear Thee a sign to flee from the face of a bow. Diapsalma.
Thou didst visit the earth and make it drunk; Thou didst multiply its enrichment. God’s river was filled with water; Thou didst prepare their food, for thus is Thy preparation.
Hear us, God our Savior, the hope of all earth’s ends and of those far away at sea,
who prepares mountains in His strength, girded with power;
who troubles the sea’s hollow, the sounds of its waves. The nations will be troubled,
and those dwelling at the ends will fear Thy signs; Thou wilt gladden the departures of morning and evening.
From Thy sanctuary over Jerusalem, kings will bring Thee gifts.
Rebuke the beasts of the reed, the assembly of bulls among the heifers of peoples, so that those tested by silver may not be shut out; scatter nations that desire wars.
Envoys will come from Egypt; Ethiopia will hasten its hand toward God.
Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; make music to the Lord. Diapsalma.
Make music to God, who rides upon the heaven of heaven toward the east; behold, He will give with His voice a voice of power.
I will praise God’s name with a song and magnify Him in praise,
and it will please God more than a young calf bringing forth horns and hoofs.
Let the poor see and rejoice; seek God, and your soul will live,
for the Lord heard the needy and did not despise His bound ones.
Let the heavens and earth praise Him, the sea and everything creeping in them.
For God will save Zion, and Judea’s cities will be built; they will dwell there and inherit it.
Why dost Thou turn away Thy hand and Thy right hand from within Thy bosom to the end?
But God is our King before the age; He worked salvation in the midst of the earth.
Thou didst strengthen the sea by Thy power; Thou didst crush the dragons’ heads upon the water.
Thou didst crush the dragon’s heads; Thou gavest him as food to the Ethiopian peoples.
Thou didst break open springs and torrents; Thou didst dry up rivers of Etham.
Thine is the day, and Thine is the night; Thou didst fashion light and the sun.
In all these things they sinned still and did not believe in His wonders,
and their days failed in futility, and their years with haste.
Whenever He killed them, they sought Him; and they returned and rose early toward God,
and remembered that God is their helper, and God Most High is their redeemer.
And they deceived Him with their mouth, and lied to Him with their tongue,
but their heart was not upright with Him, nor were they faithful in His covenant.
Make their rulers like Oreb and Zeeb, and Zebah and Zalmunna—all their rulers,
who said, “Let us inherit for ourselves the sanctuary of God.”
My God, make them like a wheel, like straw before the wind.
Like fire that will burn through a woodland, as though a flame should burn up mountains,
so Thou wilt pursue them with Thy storm and trouble them in Thy wrath.
Fill their faces with dishonor, and they will seek Thy name, Lord.
Let them be ashamed and troubled for an age of an age; let them be abashed and perish,
A psalm of David. Sing to the Lord a new song, for the Lord has done wonders. His right hand and His holy arm won salvation for Him.
The Lord made His salvation known; before the nations He revealed His righteousness.
He remembered His mercy to Jacob and His truth to the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth saw the salvation of our God.
And the Lord became a refuge for the needy, a helper at fitting times in distress.
Let those who know Thy name hope in Thee, for Thou hast not abandoned those who seek Thee, Lord.
Sing praise to the Lord, who dwells in Zion; announce His deeds among the nations,
And the Lord remains for ever; He prepared His throne for judgment,
and He will judge the inhabited world in righteousness; He will judge peoples with uprightness.
For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive, and contrary to nature were grafted into a cultivated olive, how much more will these natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree!
For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of this mystery, so that you may not be wise in your own eyes: that a partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles enters,
and in this way all Israel will be saved, just as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
And this is My covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”
With regard to the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but with regard to election, beloved for the fathers’ sake.
For God’s gifts and calling are irrevocable.
But what if God, willing to demonstrate wrath and to make His power known, endured with much patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
and did so to make known the wealth of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory,
even us whom He also called, not only from Jews but also from Gentiles?
As He also says in Hosea, “I will call those who are not My people ‘My people,’ and her who is not beloved ‘beloved’;
and in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ there they will be called sons of the living God.”
But Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, “Though the number of Israel’s sons be like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved;
for the Lord will carry out a word on the earth, completing it and cutting it short.”
Judah will draw up for battle in Jerusalem and gather the strength of all the surrounding peoples: gold, silver and clothing in very great abundance.
This will also be the downfall of horses, mules, camels, donkeys and every animal in those camps, according to this downfall.
Whoever remains from all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up each year to bow before the King, the Lord Almighty, and celebrate the Festival of Tent-Pitching.
Whoever among all the earth’s tribes does not go up to Jerusalem to bow before the King, the Lord Almighty—these will be added to those.
If Egypt’s tribe does not go up or come there, upon these too will be the downfall with which the Lord will strike all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tent-Pitching.
This will be Egypt’s sin and the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tent-Pitching.
On that day what is upon the horse’s bridle will be holy to the Lord Almighty, and the cauldrons in the Lord’s house will be like bowls before the altar.

Every cauldron in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the Lord Almighty. All who sacrifice will come, take some of them and boil in them. No Canaanite will remain in the house of the Lord Almighty on that day.
An oracle of the Lord’s word: in Sedrach’s land and Damascus is His sacrifice, because the Lord watches human beings and all Israel’s tribes,
and Emath within its borders, Tyre and Sidon, because they were exceedingly wise.
Tyre built herself fortifications, stored silver like dust and gathered gold like the mud of the roads.
Therefore the Lord will inherit her and strike her strength into the sea; she will be consumed by fire.
Ashkelon will see and fear; Gaza will suffer greatly, and Akkaron too, because she was ashamed at her downfall. A king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will certainly not be inhabited.
Foreigners will dwell in Azotus, and I will bring down the foreigners’ arrogance.
The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah, son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
Let everything utterly disappear from the face of the earth, says the Lord,
let humanity and livestock disappear, let birds of the sky and fish of the sea disappear, and I will remove people from the face of the earth, says the Lord.
I will stretch My hand against Judah and all Jerusalem’s inhabitants, and remove from this place the names of Baal and the names of the priests,
those worshiping the army of heaven on rooftops, those swearing by the Lord and those swearing by their king,
The Lord will appear against them and destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth. All the islands of the nations will worship Him, each from his place.
You too, Ethiopians, are slain by My sword.
He will stretch His hand against the north and destroy the Assyrian, making Nineveh a waterless wasteland like a wilderness.

Flocks and all the wild animals of the earth will graze within her; chameleons and hedgehogs will lie in her recessed panels. Wild animals will cry in her openings, and ravens in her gateways, for cedar is her structure.

This is the contemptuous city dwelling in confidence, saying in her heart, “I am, and there is no one after me.” How she became a wasteland, pasture for wild animals! Everyone passing through her will hiss and wave his hands.
From the far reaches of Ethiopia’s rivers they will bring sacrifices to Me.

On that day you will certainly not be ashamed of all the practices by which you acted impiously toward Me; then I will remove from you the contemptuous acts of your arrogance, and you will no longer boast upon My holy mountain.
I will leave within you a meek and humble people, and they will revere the Lord’s name,
I said, “Only fear Me and accept discipline, and you will certainly not be destroyed from her eyes,” with all I exacted upon her. Prepare, rise early! All their gleaning has been ruined.

Therefore wait for Me, says the Lord, for the day of My rising for testimony. My judgment is for assemblies of nations, to receive kings and pour all My furious wrath upon them; for all the earth will be consumed in My jealous fire.
For then I will change a tongue for peoples, for its generation, so that all call upon the Lord’s name and serve Him under one yoke.
